clue.text: Sink unit almost blocked by plug

indicators.note: blocked by means the shortened unit has the plug stuck inside it
almost means the last letter of the unit is dropped

parts.note: a degree is a unit of temperature or angle
a plug is an advertisement, an ad

explanation.surface: A kitchen sink unit is nearly jammed by its own plug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sink' looks like the kitchen fitting the surface paints, but it is the verb: to sink low.
explanation.definitionFit: To sink morally is to lower oneself, to debase or demean, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Cheat bet on woman outliving husband

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat them
a wager is a bet

explanation.surface: Someone cheats by betting on a widow's longevity.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a widow holding a title or property from her late husband.

clue.text: Field from which one obtains a better view of one's surroundings

definitions.text: Field from which one obtains a better view of one's surroundings

parts.words: Field from which one obtains a better view of one's surroundings
parts.note: sounds like a hill or vantage point, but the field is an academic subject studying landscapes and places

explanation.definitionFit: This academic discipline studies the Earth's physical features, peoples and places, so it explains one's surroundings.

clue.text: Financial backer promoting liberal point of view

indicators.note: promoting means the letter moves up, earlier in the word

parts.note: an angel is a backer of a theatrical show

explanation.surface: A financial backer is pushing a liberal standpoint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoting' moves the L of ANGEL up one place.
explanation.definitionFit: An angle is a particular perspective or slant on a matter.

clue.text: Raised the French vessel over river banks

indicators.note: banks means the turned river lies on either side of the other letters
over, in a down clue, means the river's name is turned upside down

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
le is French for the
a vat is a large container

explanation.surface: A French ship was lifted over the riverbanks.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' turns the river upward; 'banks' means it lies on both sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevated means lifted up to a higher position, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Gangster regrets bombing Revolutionary Guards

indicators.note: revolutionary means the held letters turn round and read backwards
guards means the clue words hold the letters within them

explanation.surface: A gangster regrets an attack carried out by the Iranian Revolutionary Guards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guards' holds RETSBOM inside 'regrets bombing'; 'Revolutionary' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangster is a member of a criminal mob, a straight synonym.

clue.text: New way of working beginning to rein in study

parts.note: MO is modus operandi, a way of working

indicators.note: in means that letter sits inside the study

parts.note: a den is a private study

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of the word rein

explanation.surface: A new working method that starts by curbing study.
explanation.walkthrough: MO stands for modus operandi; R goes in DEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern means up to date or recent, a synonym for new.

clue.text: Pet salesman bumped into expert from the South

indicators.note: from the South means, in a down clue, that the letters are read upwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
to bump into someone is to meet them
a dab, as in dab hand, is an expert

explanation.surface: A pet salesman ran into an expert who came up from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like an animal or a darling, but it is a fit of sulking. The pieces REP, MET and DAB are read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet is an old word for a fit of pique, a sulk or huff.

clue.text: Subject of article about what constrains empiricism

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: about means those outside letters are turned round
what constrains a word is its outermost letters, which hold the rest in

explanation.surface: The subject of a paper on the limits of empiricism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what constrains' gives the outside letters E and M; 'about' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the topic or subject of a talk or piece of writing.

clue.text: Recognition for prize-winning group stifled by mindless repetition

indicators.note: stifled by means the group is smothered inside the repetition

parts.note: rote learning is mindless repetition
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A prize-winning group whose creativity is stifled by doing the same thing over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a ribbon badge awarded to winners at shows, a mark of recognition.

clue.text: Grown-up leader somehow sensed perversity

indicators.note: up, as in stirred up, tells us to mix the letters of grown

parts.note: a leader is a head

indicators.note: somehow means the letters of sensed come out in some other order

explanation.surface: A grown-up leader somehow detected stubborn contrariness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grown-up' looks like one word for adult, but 'up' is the anagram signal working on GROWN (WRONG); 'somehow' turns SENSED into EDNESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Perversity is stubborn, misguided obstinacy, the quality of persisting in error.

clue.text: Defile girl's head soaked in blood

indicators.note: soaked in means the letter is placed inside the blood

parts.note: gore is spilt blood

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word girl's

explanation.surface: A grisly scene: a girl's head drenched in blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defile' looks like a verb, to sully, but here it is the noun, a narrow pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A defile is a narrow mountain pass or ravine, the same thing as a steep-sided valley.

clue.text: Contract staff overwhelmed by advance welcome

parts.note: a stands for ante, before, so in advance

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means the staff are swallowed up inside the welcome

parts.note: to welcome someone is to greet them
staff are workers, men

explanation.surface: Contract workers swamped by a warm reception laid on in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract is a binding deal between parties, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Cut and thrust of blade disguising skill shown by fencer ultimately

indicators.note: shown by sets the fencer's last letter beside the blade
ultimately means the final letter of the word fencer
disguising means the blade hides the skill inside it

parts.note: an epee is a fencing sword
art is skill

explanation.surface: A fencing bout where a blade conceals the swordsman's skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut and thrust' looks like swordplay in a fencing surface, but here it means verbal sparring.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut and thrust is lively verbal sparring, the witty back-and-forth of quick replies.

clue.text: Likelihood of danger goes up having family visit with son

indicators.note: visit means the family goes into the house of the rising word

parts.note: to go up is to rise, so goes up is rises
kin are family

explanation.surface: The risk rises when family come to stay with a son.
explanation.definitionFit: Riskiness is the state of being hazardous, the chance that harm may come.

clue.text: Positive aspect of winning team

parts.note: to be up is to be ahead, winning
a side is a team

explanation.surface: The good thing about a team that keeps on winning.
explanation.definitionFit: The upside of something is its good or beneficial side, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Uplifting new season, winning one after another

indicators.note: after means the inner I follows the first I

parts.note: another means a second one, so another letter I

indicators.note: winning means the new season wins, or takes in, a letter

parts.note: spring is a season
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An uplifting new season for a team winning one match after another.
explanation.walkthrough: One I goes inside N + SPRING; 'after another' puts a second I in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspiring means encouraging or rousing, giving people a lift.

clue.text: What docker did having caught dog in act

definitions.note: a docker who docks a dog cuts off its tail

indicators.note: in means the dog word goes inside the act

parts.note: a deed is an act
to dog someone is to tail them

explanation.surface: A dock worker caught a dog in the act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docker' wants to be a port worker; here it is someone who docks tails, so the dog is de-tailed.
explanation.definitionFit: Read playfully, de-tailed means relieved of a tail, as docking does to a dog.

clue.text: Nonsense about why, reportedly, I like young men

indicators.note: about means the nonsense goes around the other letters

parts.note: bosh is nonsense

indicators.note: reportedly means we hear the word why and write the letter it sounds like

parts.note: why sounds like the letter Y

explanation.surface: Someone asks why, they say, they like young men, and gets nonsense back.
explanation.definitionFit: Boyish describes what is typical of boys or youths, youthful in manner.

clue.text: Record covered by Squeeze replaced rude word?

indicators.note: covered by means the record sits inside the squeeze

parts.note: to bleed someone is to squeeze money from them
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A record cover version by the band Squeeze had a rude word swapped out.
explanation.walkthrough: Squeeze is also a British pop band, the surface's misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleeped describes a swear word censored on air with a beep sound in its place.

clue.text: Obsession with crime returning to engulf French capital?

indicators.note: to engulf means the turned crime goes around the money
returning means the word for crime is read backwards

parts.note: a sin is a crime or wrongdoing
capital as money: the currency used in France is the euro

explanation.surface: A criminal obsession with taking over Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French capital' wants to be Paris; it is the money France uses. 'returning' gives NIS, which goes round EUROS.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurosis is a mental disorder, often taking the form of a fixation or compulsive anxiety.

clue.text: Doctor remains for discussion group

indicators.note: doctor as a verb means to tamper with, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A doctor stays on for a group discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a class or meeting where a small group discusses a topic.

clue.text: Age you are said to divorce partner

indicators.note: to divorce means the partner's letters are split apart by the others

parts.note: a mate is a partner

indicators.note: said means we write what you are sounds like, the letters U and R

parts.note: you are sounds like the two letters U R

explanation.surface: As you get older, they say, you divorce your partner.
explanation.definitionFit: To age is to grow older and riper, to develop fully over time.

clue.text: Deal with China reduced fare from Mexico

indicators.note: reduced, as in reduced to pieces, signals the letters are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: A trade deal with China cuts the price of Mexican food.
explanation.definitionFit: This rolled, filled tortilla in chilli sauce is a classic dish of Mexican cuisine.

clue.text: Shot Colt pistol containing a single round

parts.note: c stands for colt in horse-racing form guides

indicators.note: containing means the pistol holds the round within it

parts.note: a pistol is a firearm, an arm
a single round thing is the letter O

explanation.surface: A Colt pistol loaded with only one bullet takes a shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colt' looks like the gunmaker; it is a young horse, C in racing.
explanation.definitionFit: A carom is a billiards shot in which the cue ball strikes two balls in turn.

clue.text: Reproach leader of party leaving platform

indicators.note: leaving means that letter departs from the platform

parts.note: a podium is a raised platform

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of the word party

explanation.surface: A party leader walks off the stage amid reproach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader of' gives P, and 'leaving' takes it out of PODIUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is disgrace or general condemnation, the reproach that attaches to a hated act.

clue.text: One divided by zero vacuously equals something elementary

indicators.note: divided by means the one is split apart by the other letters
vacuously means the word zero is emptied of its middle, leaving its outside letters

explanation.surface: A maths puzzle: one divided by zero equals something basic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elementary' means simple in the surface but here points to a chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: This gas is a form of the element oxygen, made of three atoms, so something of an element.

clue.text: Aim to turn people insane going on and on

indicators.note: insane means the letters behave crazily and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to drive people mad.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the idea of a machine that runs forever without any energy input, never stopping.

clue.text: With time, this estate could make ends meet

indicators.note: could make means the letters of ends meet are rearranged, with an extra letter in the pool

explanation.surface: Adding time, this estate might help its owners make ends meet.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer plus T are together an anagram of ENDS MEET, signalled by 'could make'.
explanation.definitionFit: A demesne is land held and worked by a lord, a landed property or manor.

clue.text: Doctor clamps right side to expose vessel

indicators.note: clamps means the doctor holds the other letters within

parts.note: an edge is a side

explanation.surface: A doctor clamps the right side of a wound to expose a blood vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' looks medical, a vein, but it is a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dredger is a ship fitted to scoop silt from the bed of a waterway.
